title: What If Heat and Humidity Hit the Limit Your Body Can Survive?

scenes.text: What if sweating stopped working? Even in the shade, you'd be in trouble.
Sweat cools you only by evaporating. At 35 degrees Celsius wet-bulb, that cooling fails.
That could be 35 degrees at one hundred percent humidity, or about 46 at fifty percent.
Your core temperature climbs, and researchers estimate a healthy person is in danger after about six hours.
It has been touched only briefly, mostly in South Asia and the Persian Gulf, never longer than two hours.
And newer lab tests suggest trouble can start closer to 31 degrees wet-bulb.

description:
What if heat and humidity reached the limit your body can survive?
At 35 degrees Celsius wet-bulb, sweat can't cool you. It has only been reached briefly, in a few places.
What should we run through next?
